name: ezPDF Reader PDF Annotate Form
complaints: Developer repeatedly abandoned the app ('abandoned it at the height of its glory, revived it when everyone had moved on, then abandoned it again for a couple of years')
Frequent crashes and performance problems on modern devices; confusing UI overhaul after long-dormant updates
Suspicious new phone/microphone permission requirements drove paying owners to uninstall
Once 'best selling, best rated' multimedia PDF annotator/form-filler — large paid install base now stranded
freeIncumbentRisk: High for plain reading (Google Drive/Xodo free), but its niche — multimedia PDF, TTS read-aloud, form filling, annotation on a one-time-purchase model — has few maintained one-time-price competitors
moatNotes: Its ratings base proves people paid $4 for offline annotate+forms+TTS. A maintained, modern-Android, one-time-purchase PDF annotator with no telemetry directly harvests this abandoned paid audience.

name: Sortly: Inventory Simplified
price: Paid-gated: free tier capped (~100 items); subscriptions ~$29-$59+/mo, users report $299/mo and $468→$1,467/yr jumps
complaints: Bait-and-switch pricing: users build large inventories on cheap plans, then face drastic renewal hikes ('held hostage' — $468 to $1,467 in 30 days after 3 years; non-profit hit with ~$4,000 increase)
Legacy subscriptions discontinued, forcing ~$500/yr or a free tier limited to 100 entries
Per-item pricing punishes home/collection users with big inventories but few transactions
Items disappearing after updates; sync bugs on larger datasets; inconsistent support
freeIncumbentRisk: Low-moderate: spreadsheets are the 'free' alternative but lack photos/barcode/folders; no dominant free visual-inventory app exists
moatNotes: Data-hostage resentment is the wedge: a photo-first inventory app with flat one-time or cheap capped pricing and full local export kills the exact fear driving 1-star reviews. Small-biz + insurance-documentation users demonstrably pay.

name: SwiftScan (formerly Scanbot Pro)
price: Paid-gated: free scans watermark-limited features; VIP subscription $22.49/yr (was $7 one-time as Scanbot Pro)
complaints: Classic forced paid→subscription migration: users who bought Scanbot Pro one-time were told to pay $4/mo subscription — 'a ludicrous money grab'
Rebrand doo→SwiftScan→Maple Media ownership churn eroded trust
Cloud upload (Drive/Dropbox), OCR and other formerly-owned features moved behind VIP paywall
Longtime pro-mode users locked out of features they had paid for
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Google Drive scan, Microsoft Lens, Adobe Scan are free and good — differentiation must be privacy/on-device OCR/one-time price, not basic scanning
moatNotes: The 61k-rating base at 3.86 shows churn-ready paying scanners; winning angle is 'buy once, offline OCR, no account, no watermark' — precisely what Scanbot originally sold before the rug-pull.

name: PDF Editor & Reader | Xodo (Apryse)
price: Paid-gated: formerly fully free; core editing/annotation features now behind subscription (~$10-12/mo tiers) after Apryse acquisition
complaints: Features that were free for nearly a decade (editing, annotation depth, e-sign volume) moved behind an aggressive subscription after Apryse/PDFTron acquisition
Subscription priced for business but pitched at everyone — 'too expensive for non-business users'
Free tier progressively shrunk (e.g. Xodo Sign document limits cut 5→3/month)
Beloved-free-app betrayal dynamic: enormous legacy user base actively hunting replacements
freeIncumbentRisk: Moderate: many free PDF viewers exist, but full-fidelity annotate/edit/fill-sign offline without account or watermark is still scarce on Android
moatNotes: Rating sits right at the 4.1 threshold but the volume is enormous (340k ratings, 130k installs/30d). A one-time-purchase 'what Xodo used to be' annotator targets a huge, articulate, already-searching audience. Biggest TAM of this list.

name: eFax App - Fax from Phone
price: Paid-gated: app useless without eFax subscription (~$16.95+/mo, setup fees)
complaints: Cancellation is deliberately convoluted: cancel button doesn't work, chat loops back to broken email link, phone cancellations 'processed' yet card keeps getting charged month after month
Continued billing after confirmed cancellation with refunds refused (2.1 stars on Sitejabber; Trustpilot/ConsumerAffairs full of identical stories)
Pricing structure perceived as misleading and exploitative for low-volume users
Customers put on indefinite hold or hung up on when requesting cancellation
freeIncumbentRisk: Low: faxing is inherently paid (telco costs); no viable free incumbent — competitors (iFax etc.) show similar billing resentment
moatNotes: Occasional-fax users (medical/legal/government forms) are massively overserved by monthly subs. Pay-per-fax with transparent pricing and instant self-serve cancellation attacks the exact 1-star driver. J2/Consensus is a legacy conglomerate slow to respond.
